description: A single rendered table, headed "Feature" (left column) and "Type" (four remaining columns), classifying low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C steels by their hot-rolled microstructure. The four type columns are labelled "Ferritic [37-43]", "Ferrite based duplex [44-60]", "Austenite based duplex [61-71]" and "Austenitic [72-87]", the bracketed values being reference numbers. Three feature rows follow. Row "Hot rolled microstructure" contains hand-drawn schematics: the Ferritic column shows only elongated, banded grains labelled δ; the Ferrite based duplex column shows elongated δ bands interleaved with a few equiaxed grains; the Austenite based duplex column shows equiaxed grains labelled δ and γ together with elongated δ; the Austenitic column shows a fully equiaxed polygonal grain network labelled γ. Row "Typical composition range" gives Al ~ 5-9 %, Mn < 5 %, C < 0.05 % (Ferritic); Al ~ 3-7 %, Mn ~ 2-12 %, C ~ 0.05-0.5 % (Ferrite based duplex); Al ~ 5-10 %, Mn ~ 5-30 %, C ~ 0.4-0.7 % (Austenite based duplex); Al ~ 5-12 %, Mn ~ 12-30 %, C ~ 0.6-2.0 % (Austenitic). Row "Tensile property" (footnote a defines UTS as ultimate tensile strength and TE as total elongation) gives UTS ~ 200-600 MPa / TE ~ 10-40 %; UTS ~ 400-900 MPa / TE ~ 10-40 %; UTS ~ 800-1300 MPa / TE ~ 10-40 %; and UTS ~ 800-1500 MPa / TE ~ 30-80 %. The table demonstrates that increasing Mn and C, converting the microstructure from banded ferrite through duplex to equiaxed austenite, progressively raises the strength and elongation window.

observations.observation: The figure is a table whose left column lists three features — Hot rolled microstructure, Typical composition range, and Tensile property — and whose remaining four columns define the steel Types: Ferritic, Ferrite based duplex, Austenite based duplex and Austenitic.
The Ferritic column schematic shows only elongated, banded grains labelled δ, i.e. a single-phase delta-ferritic hot-rolled microstructure.

The Ferrite based duplex column schematic shows elongated δ bands with a small volume fraction of equiaxed grains, whereas the Austenite based duplex column shows equiaxed grains labelled both δ and γ plus elongated δ bands.
The Austenitic column schematic shows a fully equiaxed polygonal grain structure labelled γ with no elongated δ bands.

Typical composition ranges printed in the table are: Ferritic Al ~ 5-9%, Mn < 5%, C < 0.05%; Ferrite based duplex Al ~ 3-7%, Mn ~ 2-12%, C ~ 0.05-0.5%; Austenite based duplex Al ~ 5-10%, Mn ~ 5-30%, C ~ 0.4-0.7%; Austenitic Al ~ 5-12%, Mn ~ 12-30%, C ~ 0.6-2.0%.

Tensile properties printed are: Ferritic UTS ~ 200-600 MPa and TE ~ 10-40%; Ferrite based duplex UTS ~ 400-900 MPa and TE ~ 10-40%; Austenite based duplex UTS ~ 800-1300 MPa and TE ~ 10-40%; Austenitic UTS ~ 800-1500 MPa and TE ~ 30-80%.

The table shows that strength increases monotonically across the classification sequence Ferritic → Ferrite based duplex → Austenite based duplex → Austenitic, while the largest total elongation window (30-80%) occurs only for the fully Austenitic type.
Footnote a defines the abbreviations used in the tensile property row: UTS = ultimate tensile strength and TE = total elongation.
The caption states this figure classifies low density steels according to hot rolled microstructures.
The type column headers carry bracketed reference numbers — [37-43], [44-60], [61-71] and [72-87] — indicating the literature sources compiled for each class.
Mn content rises from < 5% for the Ferritic type to 12-30% for the Austenitic type, tracking the transition from banded δ-ferrite to equiaxed γ-austenite microstructures.
